title: Travel: Paul McCartney – Nashville to New York | 1974
content:
Wings left Nashville, Tennessee, on 18 July 1974.

They had been in the city for several weeks, working on new songs and rehearsing potential live numbers. They rehearsed and stayed at a farm owned by songwriter Claude ‘Curly’ Putman Jr, who wanted their home back.

Denny Laine, Jimmy McCulloch, and Geoff Britton flew back to London at 2.45pm. Paul and Linda McCartney, meanwhile, asked the Putmans if they and their children could stay longer, but their request was declined.

Instead, they rented a car and truck, and hit the road, beginning a long drive to New York. They arrived in Knoxville for their first stop later that evening. In New York they stayed at Linda’s family’s summer house in East Hampton.
